statement: In 194 healthy, screened volunteers aged 18 to 45, four in five new to MDMA, who took MDMA by mouth lying in a quiet hospital ward in Basel, with a placebo on another day (10 double-blind crossover studies pooled by the laboratory that ran them; a single dose in each analysed session, 125 mg for 164 people and 75 mg for 30, the same for women and men, as study conditions; 112 of them also took MDMA in another session after a medicine given first, which was not analysed; Studerus et al., 2021), the amount taken per kilogram of body weight and the blood level went most with how strongly the effects were felt, as the volunteers rated them. Without adjustment, the blood level was associated with the rating of any drug effect (standardized beta 0.48), and in penalized models dose per kilogram was selected for 21 of 25 effects and ranked first for 12, among them any drug effect, good drug effect, high mood, feeling stimulated and liking, but mattered less for unpleasant or anxious reactions. At the same dose per kilogram, genetically lower activity of the liver enzyme CYP2D6 went with a higher blood level (beta −0.19), older age with a smaller rise in heart rate (−0.27), higher openness with more closeness to others (0.28) and oceanic boundlessness (0.22), higher neuroticism (rated at screening) and trait anxiety with more dread of ego dissolution (0.32 each) and impaired control (0.26 each), and a more anxious-depressed or introverted mood just before the dose with more anxiety (0.25 and 0.23); oceanic boundlessness, dread of ego dissolution, impaired control and anxiety were rated on a questionnaire at the end of the session, looking back over it. Each of these associations survived correction for multiple testing and was modest, explaining 5 to 12% of the variation (semi-partial R2). For a rating of a bad drug effect, older age, trait anxiety and anxious-depressed mood before the dose ranked highest in the penalized models, but the association with age did not survive correction for multiple testing in the main models. Women and men did not differ significantly once dose per kilogram was allowed for; because everyone took a fixed amount and women weighed less, women received more per kilogram, so sex and dose per kilogram went together and cannot be cleanly separated in these data (dose per kilogram varied from 0.8 to 2.7 mg/kg across the volunteers). The authors note that this does not confirm earlier studies that found differences between women and men even after adjusting for body weight, and they cite others, among them an earlier report on safety data from these studies (Vizeli and Liechti, 2017), suggesting that women may be more prone to unpleasant effects, while a three-laboratory study of 220 people detected no differences between women and men. Previous MDMA use showed no association, but no one had used it more than five times before the study. Expectations were not among the measures, and the setting, highly standardized, could not be studied. So differences between bodies went with feeling more or less from the same amount: at a fixed amount a lighter body meant more per kilogram, which went with stronger effects, and genetically lower enzyme activity went with a higher blood level; each analysed session had one fixed dose, so what happens when someone who feels little takes more was not tested here (controlled studies of a second dose are covered in a separate answer). Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
plain: In laboratory studies of healthy young adults, how much MDMA they got for their body weight, and how much reached the blood, went most with how strongly they felt it. People with more anxious personalities, or who felt anxious and low just before, said at the end of the session that they had felt more anxious, and more open people felt closer to others; these links were modest. Women and men did not clearly differ once body weight was allowed for, although an earlier report from the same laboratory suggested women may feel more unpleasant effects. Each session had one fixed amount, so what happens when someone who feels little takes more was not tested.
population: Healthy, screened adults aged 18 to 45, mostly new to MDMA, given MDMA in a hospital ward in 10 pooled laboratory studies (194 people)
exposure: Dose per kilogram and, without adjustment, blood level; characteristics measured before dosing: sex, age, CYP2D6 genetic activity score, previous MDMA use, personality at screening, trait anxiety (timing not stated) and mood just before the dose
comparator: Volunteers with lower or higher values of each characteristic, at the same dose per kilogram (placebo sessions in the same people)
outcome: Self-rated and physical effects of MDMA (visual analogue scales over the session; 5D-ASC rated at the end of the session, looking back; Adjective Mood Rating Scale; blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, blood level)
magnitude: Unadjusted: blood level and any drug effect beta 0.48. Penalized models: dose per kilogram selected for 21 of 25 responses, first for 12. Adjusted for dose per kilogram and corrected for multiple testing: CYP2D6 genetic activity score and blood level −0.19 (R2 0.10); age and heart-rate rise −0.27 (R2 0.07); openness and closeness 0.28 (R2 0.08), oceanic boundlessness 0.22 (R2 0.06); neuroticism and trait anxiety and dread of ego dissolution 0.32 each (R2 0.12 and 0.11), impaired control 0.26 each; anxious-depressed and introverted mood before the dose and 5D-ASC anxiety 0.25 and 0.23 (R2 0.06 and 0.05). Age and bad drug effect: first in the penalized model, not significant after correction. Sex and previous MDMA use (at most five times): no significant association after adjustment.

risk_of_bias.note: Some concerns (card sc_studerus_2021): each predictor adjusted only for dose per kilogram, correlated predictors not adjusted for one another, blinding probably did not hold at 125 mg, the text does not say whether ratings were placebo-corrected, so rating style could add to trait-rating associations, and the 5D-ASC ratings were made at the end of the session, looking back.

inconsistency.note: One pooled analysis. On sex, the authors cite an earlier report on safety data from these studies (Vizeli and Liechti, 2017) among studies suggesting women may be more prone to unpleasant effects; the two analyses share most of their data and are not independent, so this is stated in the claim rather than rated as inconsistency.

indirectness.note: Worded for healthy laboratory volunteers taking one known dose; real-life use is named as different in the statement.

imprecision.note: 194 people; corrected significance throughout; modest variance shares stated.

publication_bias.note: All 500 adjusted tests are said to be displayed and corrected.

grade.reasoning: The MDMA-placebo contrast was randomized in each source study, but which person's characteristics predict the response is a between-person, observational question, so it starts low; down one for risk of bias, giving very low. Status single study: one pooled analysis from one laboratory; other Basel pooled analyses share these source studies and its LSD counterpart shares one study and several authors, so they are not independent confirmation. On sex, the answer on what MDMA feels like reports the earlier analysis (higher bad-effect ratings in women after allowing for dose per kilogram); in the editors' reading the difference may come from the outcome measure (area under the effect curve here, peak ratings there) and from the correction for multiple testing applied here, and it is listed for the senior author.
